payload.goal: Make sofar improve itself without breaking its invariants: (L1) zero-model local adaptation from outcome signals already in the record, proposed rather than applied, reversible, local-only (never telemetry); (L2) sofar improve, where the operator's own agent via sofar drive patches one ranked loss at a time, is never auto-merged, and cannot touch the checksummed evaluator; (L3) a release gate on held-out lead margin over the best current competitor (bench-refresh D19). Starts with outcome capture: tool errors and exit codes.

payload.text: Audit 2026-09-15: core/cursor.ts exportEvents exports every envelope-valid event, and client/push.ts pushes that stream without event-type privacy filtering. The hook intentionally excludes self-recording git/sofar commands; CommandRunPayload currently carries only cmd, and MCP rejections return errors without outcome events. A miner cannot treat missing outcomes, calls or memory-use evidence as zero, and never-synced diagnostics cannot simply be appended to initiative events.jsonl.

Audit checkpoint: self-improve remains 0/11 with no gating Decisions recorded and no tune/improve commands implemented in main. Priority design findings: (1) proposed miner metrics exceed existing event observability; (2) local-only diagnostics conflict with exporting all events and cannot be stored as disposable derived indexes if they are the only evidence; (3) offline replay validates rendering, not causal model behavior; (4) checksums and writable-worktree diff checks do not isolate the evaluator; (5) proposal approval/application/reversion, durable budgets and an immutable supervisor need explicit contracts; (6) repeated held-out lead gates risk test-set overfitting; (7) compare full improvement-loop cost against matched-budget simpler baselines. Findings are advisory, not new Decisions.
